title: Kanni, Hot Sauce for Accara
author: Marie-Claude Mendy, Chef and Owner of Teranga (Oldways)
desc: Onions cooked in olive oil, tomato paste, water, habaneros, a splash of white vinegar and cayenne simmered about 20 minutes, then finished with a spoonful and a half of nokkos garlic paste — the hot sauce served beside accara.
longDesc: Chef Marie-Claude Mendy’s kanni is made in two parts. The nokkos — Senegalese garlic paste — is a puree of garlic, bell pepper, green onions, yellow onion, salt, pepper and cayenne. The sauce is built in a pan: green and yellow onions cooked in olive oil about 5 minutes, tomato paste added and cooked 3 to 4 minutes over medium heat, then water, black pepper, chopped habaneros, white vinegar and cayenne added and the heat lowered for about 20 minutes. One and a half tablespoons of the nokkos are stirred in at the end. Served beside accara, or spread on baguette slices as sandwiches. The page’s stated total time of 10 minutes cannot be squared with its method (about 29 minutes of stated cooking); both are recorded and not reconciled.
ingredients: 1 bell pepper, cubed — size not printed
1 bunch green onions — size not printed
Pepper — quantity and type not printed
2 habanero peppers, finely chopped (or another hot pepper)
Salt, to taste — quantity not printed
steps: Process the garlic, bell pepper, green onions and yellow onion in a food processor with the salt, pepper and cayenne until pureed. No time and no yield are printed for the nokkos; you will use only 1 1/2 tablespoons of it.
Heat the olive oil in a medium pan. Cook the green and yellow onions, stirring occasionally, about 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste.
Keep cooking over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add the water, black pepper, habaneros, white vinegar and cayenne. Lower the heat and cook about 20 minutes. Stir in 1 1/2 tablespoons of the nokkos.
Season with salt to taste. Serve beside accara, or spread on baguette slices to make sandwiches.
chefTips: The only printed cue for the nokkos is ‘until pureed’; the sauce has times, not cues.
The page prints a total time of 10 minutes; the steps add up to about 29, so plan for the longer figure.
The page uses the spelling ‘nokkos’ in the ingredient heading and ‘Nokoss’ in step 4; both are the same garlic paste.
commonMistakes: Trusting the 10-minute total on the page.
Adding the whole batch of nokkos instead of the 1 1/2 tablespoons the recipe calls for.
Confusing this nokkos with nokoss (SEN012), the onion-and-nététou base.
reheating: Serve warm or at room temperature.
healthBenefits: Habanero adds capsaicin; olive oil is the only fat.
culturalNote: The nokkos is made here as a stand-alone paste, then used by the spoonful in the sauce. Spelling is unsettled across sources — nokkos (Mendy, Ba), nokos (Thiam), nokoss — and the preparations differ; they are recorded as separate entries.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Kanni: Hot Sauce for Accara’. Byline as printed: ‘Marie-Claude Mendy, Chef and Owner of Teranga’, published by Oldways. Date: not stated. Yield 8 servings. Printed prep time 10 minutes, total time 10 minutes. SINGLE-PASS.

TIME CONTRADICTION, reported as printed and not reconciled: stated total 10 minutes vs a method containing about 20 minutes of simmering plus about 5 and 3–4 minutes of earlier cooking. The cook figure above (29) adds the three printed cooking times (5 + 4 + 20), taking the 3–4 minute step at its upper figure.
Misprints reported as printed, not fixed: ‘¼ teaspoons’ black pepper and ‘1 teaspoons’ white vinegar. The page spells the paste ‘nokkos’ in the ingredient heading and ‘Nokoss’ in step 4.
ABSENT, not estimated: the size of the bell pepper and the bunches of green onions, the amounts of salt and pepper in the nokkos, and the yield and time of the nokkos.
